Hacknet is a smart and challenging indie game. It immediately stands out as an extraordinary (yet at sometimes unrealistic) hacking simulator. The game compels you to use your head, wits, and ingenuity to solve a series of puzzles, that only seems to get deeper the farther you progress in the game, leading to a climactic and satisfying finale. Short and sweet. I played [b]Uplink[/b] back in the day, and while that was Hacking By Hollywood this is the far grittier reboot.

You hack, mostly by typing commands in a terminal window. Yes, it's repetitive, but so's holding down the trigger in [b]CoD[/b]. There's a story. There's a lot of snooping possible, by reading up on files and peoples emails... if you're into the peeping Tom thing on fictional persons.

One gripe is that near the end I had trouble knowing what the actual objective was, so I was hacking along, hacking hacking hacking, decyphering shit, going at it, all without realizing that the mission I was working one was already done. I just had to deliver the right intel to the questgiver.

Soundtrack's excellent. It looks awesome, in its hackery minimalistic way.

10/10. Would hack again.

I knew about this when it came out, but held off buying it. I don't know why. Why didn't someone tell me how goddamn great this game is?

This is how it started, after stumbling through the tutorial:

OK my first task, I have to get into some guy's computer. Not really sure I remember what to do from the tutorial but let's see how we go. 

The first thing that happens is I get to the guy's login/password. I don't have his login and password and I have no idea what to do. Er, I guess I'll do some random port scanning etc. I do some sort of scan and BAM I give myself admin access! OK now what? Er, I click around a bit and find that login. Except this time, the details I just hacked are right there! I enter the login, enter, I enter the password, enter.

And I'm IN. Like a godamn hacker. Like the goddamn elite hacker that I am. I raise my hands and twiddle my fingers like there's fire coming out of them, because that's what just happened. The matrix style music augments it.

I continue on with my hacking and similar scenarios just keep hacking and every time I accomplish something BAM I download the shiz and there's more fire coming out of my fingertips.

I have to end this now because I can't wait to keep hacking some more.
This was very good.  Intuitive, manageable, challenging, and not so long as to be too drawn out.  4/5, would play again.

Hacknet is the spiritual successor to Introversion Software's 2001 game Uplink. You start with simple "hack into X and get Y" gameplay but quickly progress to more complicated systems and detective work. The game uses real command line prompts and correct ports, plus it has a fantastic soundtrack and lots of funny files to find if you're thorough when you dig around other people's machines.

I just couldn't stop playing this game. If you're familiar with Linux prompt commands, this will be an easier game for you. However, it will still be enjoyable for the lore, the humour, and exploring folders and files outside the main story.

This is mainly a text based game, but the UI is well laid out.  You can do most of the accessing through text commands but clicking through folder hierarchies to access files is also possible and quicker (speed is a factor at times).

The story is rich and well written enough to want to know more about the characters involved. This makes the contracts seem more fleshed out instead of just doing hacker jobs for the sake of it like in Uplink, which I assume is the inspiration for this game. And some contracts are challenging enough to keep things interesting gameplay wise; akin to Portal where when you figure out a puzzle you feel clever for the accomplishment.

I'm really picky with games and rarely play through them completely, but Hacknet had me hooked from start to finish. I highly recommend it.

TLDR;

Hacknet comes down to running a few exploits, DDoS the proxy server, bypassing the firewall, and grats your in.

*  Asthetically pleasing interface
*  Marginally authentic hacking process
*  Well developed and compelling story line
*  Casual game play

----------

Pros:

I really enjoy the fact that the interface authentically portrays a Linux or Unix environment.  The interface is very authentic.  Especially if you use window managers rather than a full desktop environment.  The requirement to use the terminal instead of clicking everything makes the game feel more like real world hacking.  The Hacknet story line is more developed than other hacking simulators.  There is a sense of freedom to pick diversified contracts and to complete them however fit.  All of this supports casual game play.

Cons:

(More of a preference than a con.)

Breaking the security of a real world network devices requires time, caution, ability, and patience.  People with InfoSec experience will feel like they are rolling their face on the keyboard.  It would be nice if the game was a bit more difficult and more accurately portrayed real world hacking.
